english.title: Rendering food injurious to health with intent to sell for human consumption
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) rendered food, namely **(..SPECIFY FOOD..), injurious to health by

(A)_[adding an article or substance, namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE OR ARTICLE..), to it]_
(B)_[using an article or substance, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE OR SUBSTANCE..), as an ingredient in the preparation of it]_
(C)_[abstracting a constituent, namely **(..SPECIFY CONSTITUENT..), from it]_
(D)_[subjecting it to a process or treatment, namely **(..SPECIFY PROCESS OR TREATMENT..),]_

with intent that it should be sold for human consumption
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 7(1) and 35(2) of the Food Safety Act 1990.

other.penalty:
Either way Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine. The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
